learning_outcomes.text: Ability to solve mathematical problems that may arise in engineering.

Aptitude to apply knowledge on: linear algebra; geometry; differential geometry; differential and integral calculus; differential and partial differential equations; numerical methods; numerical algorithms; statistics and optimization.
Applies data processing and analysis techniques.
Knows the fundamental concepts, applications, and results of probability.
Understands the concepts of one-dimensional and multi-dimensional random variables.
Masters the modeling of engineering environments under stochastic nature using random variables and their applications in uncertainty situations.
Knows how to use statistical hypothesis tests and their application in decision-making.
Has the ability to prepare, understand, and critique reports based on statistical analyses.

syllabus_topics: Module 1: Exploratory data analysis in the computer lab.
Module 3: Sampling, estimation, and hypothesis testing.
Two-dimensional descriptive statistics: Regression and correlation.
Probability distributions of discrete and continuous random variables.
Confidence intervals: means, variances, and proportions.
Tests for equality of means, variances, and proportions. ANOVA. p-value calculation.
teaching_methods: Lectures on theory and examples motivating its utility in engineering

assessment_methods.method: Exam on Computer Lab practical content
Statistical Report applying various statistical techniques

assessment_rules: The final grade is composed of Exam 1 (40%), Exam 2 (20%), Computer Lab Exam (20%), and Statistical Report (20%). To pass the 60% component (Exams 1 and 2), students must score at least 4 out of 10 on each and have a weighted average of at least 4.5. To pass the 40% component (Computer Lab Exam and Statistical Report), students must score at least 4 out of 10 on each and have an average of at least 5. The overall final grade must be at least 5 out of 10 to pass. A global evaluation test equivalent to all four components is available for those who do not complete or pass the continuous assessment.
